output_json.patch_notes: In Copy.java, immediately after constructing `File f = new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())`, the fix computes the canonical paths of both the destination directory and the resolved file. If the resolved file's canonical path is neither equal to the destination nor a descendant (prefix + File.separator), an IOException "Archive entry outside of destination directory" is thrown before any directory is created or file is written. This blocks traversal entries (e.g. `../pwned.txt`) while preserving normal extraction of well-formed entries. Added CopyTest#testCopyDirectoryFromPodRejectsPathTraversal which overrides only the Exec transport to feed a base64(gzip(tar)) archive with a `../pwned.txt` entry (mirroring the POV) and asserts no file is written outside the destination directory. All 3 CopyTest tests pass and the util module builds successfully.
output_json.risk_notes: The fix uses getCanonicalPath(), which resolves symlinks and normalizes paths; this is the standard containment approach and matches the check the POV uses to detect escapes. Legitimate archives whose entries stay within the destination are unaffected. Behavior change: previously malicious entries were silently written outside destination; now they raise an IOException, aborting the copy — this is the intended hardening and callers already handle IOException from this method. Directory entries are now also validated (previously only file entries reached mkdirs), which is a strict improvement. No dependencies changed.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in io.kubernetes.client.Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod. The extraction loop built each output file with `new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())` using the fully attacker-controlled tar entry name and no containment check, so a malicious pod could supply an entry like `../pwned.txt` to write outside the destination directory. Added a canonical-path containment check that throws IOException when a resolved entry escapes the destination directory, and added a regression test that drives the real extraction path with a malicious archive.
